messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach (streaming stalls) on dedicated-pool-eu-west-1. >90% pool saturation, queue depth rising. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): on it. seeing a ton of streaming stalls in the dashboard. p95 up ~600ms -> p95 1.2s, p99 spiking to 6-8s. Starting triage.

sam (sre): adding graphs: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streams/dedicated-eu-west (posted). queue depth jumped from ~2k -> 12k over 3m. hotshot pools show 90%+ GPU utilization. autoscaler not adding nodes fast enough — warmup handshake lag ~90s.

eng-runtime: probable warmup/coldstart amplification. Handshake/backpressure path is delaying slot assignment. Streaming requests hold until KV cache warms, causing tail latency. Also seeing tokenization CPU while waiting for GPU warmup.

maria (oncall): impact? any customers seeing 5xxs?

support-ops: Yes — Acme Corp ingest pipeline reports streaming disconnects and 503s (~30% of their requests last 10m). NovaPay reports elevated retries. Customer-facing SRE notified.

ops: Temp mitigation options: 1) divert traffic to hotshot pool in us-east temporarily, 2) throttle non-urgent embed requests, 3) manual scale up dedicated pool (force warmup). Which do we want?

alex (product): prioritize customer-facing requests. Diverting to us-east might add latency for EU users but keeps SLA. Recommend divert + manual scale.

sam (sre): I'm going to execute manual scale and warmup script. Running: ```
# force-add 4 nodes to dedicated-pool-eu-west-1
redwood-cli pool resize --pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 --add 4 --reason "mitigation: warmup lag"
# pre-warm replicas
redwood-cli pool warmup --pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 --model redwood-v2-small --replicas 4
```

eng-runtime: also pushing a temporary routing policy to prefer hotshot if queue_depth>2000. Patch: ```
PATCH /routing/policies/streaming
{ "condition": "queue_depth > 2000", "action": "route:hotshot-eu | fallback:us-east" }
```

maria (oncall): doing live traffic changes now. Applying routing policy.

ops: applied token-leaky-bucket throttles for low-priority customers. Reduced concurrency for non-enterprise plans by 50%.

support-ops: customer impact note -> Acme Corp ticket #INC-8276, NovaPay -> #INC-8277. Logged errors and correlation ids.

li (eng-ml): quick model-level mitigation: suggest fall back to quantized redwood-v2-xq for streaming endpoints where latency matters. Alex ok with fallback?

alex (product): ok to fallback for non-premium routes. Keep enterprise pinned to gold pool.

sam (sre): after manual scale + warmup, p95 dropped to ~350ms within 180s, p99 trending down from 6s -> 1.1s. Queue depth halting growth at ~3.2k. Streaming stalls decreasing.

maria (oncall): confirm: manual nodes online and warm. Any residual errors?

support-ops: Acme sees error rate down to normal within 5m of routing change + scale. NovaPay retried automatically, back to baseline. No new customer reports.

eng-runtime: root cause hypothesis: burst of requests + many cold model variants caused autoscaler handshake/warmup to be rate-limited by kernel selection path. Autoscaler ramp policy uses step-up cooldown 60s which plus warmup ~90s produced cumulative delay. Need to revisit warmup parallelism and handshake timeout.

maria (oncall): immediate mitigation summary posted to incident channel. I'll create a follow-up ticket to tune autoscaler step policy and to add pre-warm heuristics for large bursts. Action items: [ENG-RUNTIME] adjust warmup parallelism, [AUTOSCALER] reduce step cooldown for high-priority customers, [PLATFORM] add predictive warmup for scheduled bursts.

sam (sre): collecting logs and traces for postmortem. dumping KV coldpath traces: ```
trace_id: ab12cd34
span: handshake -> warmup -> kv-load (heavy)
```

maria (oncall): handing off to incident review. Paging cleared. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity P1 -> mitigated; handoff to incident-review channel. Summary: dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 saturation + autoscale warmup delay => p99 spike & streaming stalls. Mitigations: manual scale + pre-warm + routing diversion + throttles. Postmortem assigned to ENG-RUNTIME and AUTOSCALER teams.

maria (oncall): adding owners: @eng-runtime (li), @autoscaler-team (sam), @platform (ops). Will schedule RCA next 48h.
